competitors.name: Wegmans / Amore
competitors.action: Wegmans launched a restaurant-inspired Amore frozen pizza line with Roman-style fermented crusts and multiple premium toppings, signaling that grocers are still pushing store-exclusive premium frozen pizza concepts instead of relying only on legacy national brands.

competitors.name: Food Lion
competitors.action: Food Lion expanded its private-label frozen pizza line across more than 1,100 stores, which is a strong shelf-pressure signal that retailer-owned frozen pizza is still scaling on assortment and value, not just holding ground during inflation.

trends.topic: The frozen pizza middle is getting squeezed from both ends
trends.magnitude: Private label is strengthening at value while premium frozen keeps sharpening its quality and differentiation cues
trends.context: Frozen pizza is increasingly behaving like a barbell category. Retailer labels are getting more credible and normalized, while premium products keep winning with better ingredients, cleaner positioning, and stronger emotional hooks. Mid-tier branded pizza is under the most pressure.

breaking.headline: Today’s clearest Real Dough signal is sharper shelf polarization, premium store exclusives up top and stronger private label pressure underneath
breaking.impact: Wegmans is investing in a more chef-inspired premium frozen pizza story while Food Lion is expanding retailer-owned pizza assortment at scale. At the same time, broader frozen-category analysis says the middle is getting crushed. For Real Dough, that means a blurry mid-tier position is the dangerous place to be.
